start.title: You already use AI. You do not need to become an AI researcher.
start.lead: For quality engineers at Samsung Display Vietnam (SDV) and DSC (China site). Scoring AI is not drafting AI. A fluent sentence is not a fact.
intro: Quality work already sits on AI: Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) scores a panel, a limit holds a lot, a report explains a claim. Generative AI — local Large Language Models (LLMs) such as Qwen, Kimi, or GLM running inside the company — drafts language. It does not replace inspection.
You do not need to train a net or pick a learning rate. You need three distinctions: a score is not a sentence, a fluent sentence is not a fact, and a local model is not a public chatbot.

whoItems.title: Quality engineers
whoItems.body: Incoming, in-process, Outgoing Quality Control (OQC), customer claims, Eight Disciplines (8D), Nonconformance Report (NCR). You own the class, the number, and the signature — not the model.

whoItems.title: Engineers, not AI specialists
whoItems.body: You can read a control chart and a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). You do not need to explain back-propagation.

whoItems.title: SDV and DSC
whoItems.body: Samsung Display Vietnam (SDV) and DSC (China site). Korean SOP, local shop cards. Same rules on both sites.

start.kindsLead: Rules decide. Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) score. Generative AI drafts. Mixing them is how a caption becomes a fake Critical Dimension (CD).

kinds.name: Rules
kinds.body: If CD is over spec, hold the lot. Interlocks, recipes, Statistical Process Control (SPC). No learning. Still the last word on a running tool.
kinds.line: A chatbot does not override an interlock.

kinds.name: Scoring AI (ML / DL)
kinds.body: The model has seen many examples and returns a class or a number: mura vs particle, risk score, remaining life. AOI and Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) live here.
kinds.line: This is the system of record for pass/fail on a panel.

kinds.name: Drafting AI (generative)
kinds.body: The model writes what did not exist: an 8D shell, a translation, a hypothesis list. Qwen, Kimi, and GLM do this job. A human still signs.
kinds.line: Fluent is not the same as true. Every number needs SOP, a Manufacturing Execution System (MES), or a gauge.

start.weekLead: You do not need a new Key Performance Indicator (KPI) named “AI usage.” You need fewer hours on first drafts and zero invented specs in a customer file.

weekItems.title: Inspection
weekItems.body: AOI still classifies the panel. Generative AI may describe a photo as a hypothesis. It may not close the lot.

weekItems.title: 8D and NCR
weekItems.body: 8D is the Eight Disciplines form for a claim or NCR. Paste the log and the SOP excerpt into the local model. Ask for D1–D3 only. You fill D4–D8 from data.

weekItems.title: Customer claims
weekItems.body: Draft a timeline and a question list. Do not let the model invent a containment date or a parts-per-million (ppm) figure.

limits.title: AI is a tool with a job. Outside that job it is noise or risk.
limits.lead: Before prompts and models: what scoring AI can do, what it cannot, then the same for generative AI. Quality owns the signature either way.
intro: “AI” in a factory is not one thing. Scoring AI (ML / DL) maps a repeating signal to a class or a number. Generative AI writes language, images, or code that did not exist. Mixing the two is how a caption becomes a fake CD.
limits.aiTitle: AI in general — scoring, rules, and drafts together
limits.aiLead: This column is the whole stack: interlocks, Automated Optical Inspection (AOI), Fault Detection and Classification (FDC), and a local Large Language Model (LLM). Useful. Not magic.

aiCan.title: Score a repeating defect
aiCan.body: AOI that has seen your mura library can class a panel photo. That is a trained job, not a chat.

aiCan.title: Flag a tool that is walking
aiCan.body: FDC learns a healthy envelope. It fires when traces leave it — often still inside spec.

aiCan.title: Rank work for a scarce hour
aiCan.body: Which ten lots to re-inspect. Which chamber to look at first. A queue, not a verdict.

aiCan.title: Draft language after the score
aiCan.body: Once AOI or a log exists, a model can write the 8D shell or the translation. Draft only.

aiNot.title: Replace an interlock or a spec
aiNot.body: If CD > spec, hold the lot. A model does not get a vote on a running tool.

aiNot.title: Stay right after the process moves
aiNot.body: A classifier trained on last year’s stack silently rots after lighting, material, or recipe change. Someone must retrain.

aiNot.title: Be accountable to the customer
aiNot.body: A named engineer signs the ppm, the date, and the containment. The model does not.

aiNot.title: Know what the chamber did at 3 a.m.
aiNot.body: Site knowledge is the review the stack is missing. AI does not walk the bay.

aiNot.title: Invent a limit that is not in SOP
aiNot.body: If the number is not in MES, SOP, or a gauge, it is not a number. It is a guess in your font.

limits.genTitle: Generative AI only — Qwen, Kimi, GLM, and anything that writes
limits.genLead: Generation is a first draft. It is the wrong tool for pass/fail, metrology, and change control.

genCan.title: Write D1–D3 of an 8D
genCan.body: 8D = Eight Disciplines. From a log and an SOP excerpt you pasted. Leave D4–D8 as questions you fill from data.

genCan.title: Turn a night of alarms into hypotheses
genCan.body: Three causes, each with a check. Mark what is missing. You kill the weak ones.

genCan.title: Translate a shop card
genCan.body: With every number, unit, tool ID, and revision frozen. Ambiguity stays in parentheses.

genCan.title: Describe a defect photo as a hypothesis
genCan.body: Likely class and why. What the photo cannot tell you. Production class still comes from AOI.

genCan.title: Draft code or SQL against a schema you gave it
genCan.body: On a copy of the extract. Read the code. Never write credentials to production.

genNot.title: Give a production pass / fail
genNot.body: That is AOI (deep learning), with gold labels and an overkill/escape threshold you chose.

genNot.title: Read CD, luminance, or ppm off a caption
genNot.body: Pretty descriptions are not metrology. Numbers come from the instrument or MES.

genNot.title: Close change control or download a recipe
genNot.body: A fluent DOE is still a process change when you run it. Existing approval path only.

genNot.title: Remember this week’s SOP by itself
genNot.body: Without retrieval it improvises. With a stale index it quotes last quarter fluently.

genNot.title: Keep a customer claim safe on a public chatbot
genNot.body: Even “just to try.” Local models only. If they are down, wait.

limits.testTitle: A thirty-second test before you send
testItems: Would I still send this if the model vanished tomorrow? If no, you have not checked it.
Is this a score from AOI / FDC / MES, or a sentence from a chat?
Every number: SOP revision, MES, or gauge — or a blank.
If this is pass/fail on a panel, the generative model is the wrong tool.
If a customer name is in the prompt, it left the public internet. Use Qwen / Kimi / GLM on site.
limits.close: A score is not a sentence. A fluent sentence is not a fact. Quality owns the signature either way.

tools.title: Use Qwen, Kimi, or GLM. Not a public chatbot.
tools.lead: On site you can run local large language models. They draft. They do not inspect. They do not get to see a public internet log of your recipe.
intro: Public ChatGPT-class tools are trained and logged outside the company. A customer claim, a stack, or an operator ID does not belong there — even “just to try.”
Qwen, Kimi, and GLM are the on-site assistants. Pick by job, not by hype. All three still hallucinate. Local only means the text stays inside. It does not mean the text is true.
If your site IT points you at a slightly different internal name, the rule does not change: approved local model, no public paste, human sign-off.

whyItems.title: Claims and customer names
whyItems.body: A complaint file identifies a brand. That is leakage the moment it hits a public log.

whyItems.title: SOP and limits
whyItems.body: Abort limits and shop cards are site knowledge. Local models can search them. Public models should never see them.

whyItems.title: Photos of panels
whyItems.body: A defect photo can still reveal stack, product, or customer. Keep vision prompts on the approved local tool.

whyItems.title: Audit
whyItems.body: When quality is asked “which assistant drafted this 8D?”, the answer should be a site tool, not a personal account.

tools.modelsLead: Capabilities overlap. This is a quality-engineer cheat sheet, not a vendor scorecard. Confirm the exact build with site IT.

models.name: Qwen
models.good: General assistant. Strong multilingual (ZH, EN, KO, VI-capable), code, tables, mixed documents.
models.quality: Default for 8D shells, yield-table questions, and KO/ZH/VI/EN drafts in one thread.

models.name: Kimi
models.good: Long documents in one go: full SOP chapter, a week of alarm logs, a claim pack with several PDFs.
models.quality: Default when the evidence is long. Paste the pack, ask it to quote revision IDs, then cut.

models.name: GLM
models.good: Strong Chinese, solid bilingual ZH–EN, structured answers. Natural fit at DSC.
models.quality: Default for Chinese shop-floor cards, DSC claim replies, and ZH SOP excerpts that must stay exact.

tools.pickTitle: Which model for which quality job

pickRows.why: Short evidence. Need a tight shell, not a novel.

pickRows.job: Read a long SOP or a full claim pack
pickRows.why: Long context. Ask it to cite the revision, then verify.
ZH first. Freeze numbers. Keep tool IDs in English.

pickRows.job: KO → VI translation of a short SOP
pickRows.why: Multilingual default. Still freeze 2.50 mm as 2.50 mm.
Hypothesis only. Production class still comes from AOI.
If the local tool is down, wait. Do not “just this once.”

tools.checkTitle: Still true on a local model
checks: Every number in a customer or line document has SOP / MES / gauge behind it.
D4–D8 of an 8D are not closed by the model.
A caption is not CD, luminance, or ppm.
You can name which local model drafted the text.
You would still send this to a customer if the model vanished tomorrow — because you checked it.
tools.neverTitle: Do not do this even on Qwen / Kimi / GLM
neverItems: Dump a full MES extract with operator IDs “so it has context.”
Ask the model for a production pass/fail on a panel.
Let it invent a containment date, a ppm, or a customer promise.
Treat “the model said so” as change control.
Fall back to a public chatbot when the local one is slow.
tools.close: Local means the text stays inside. It does not mean the text is true.

ai.title: ML, DL, and generative AI are not the same tool
ai.lead: On a display line, one kind of AI scores a panel. Another writes the deviation report. Using the wrong one wastes time and creates risk.
intro: You already work with AI even if nobody calls it that. Statistical Process Control (SPC) limits, Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) models, and Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) classifiers are machine learning or deep learning: they map a repeating signal to a score or a class.
Generative AI does a different job. It produces language, images, code, and candidate structures that did not exist before. Agentic systems sit on top and call tools.
This page is the split you need before any factory use-case. Detect versus draft. Score versus explain. Model ops versus a prompt plus a reviewer.
ai.stackTitle: The stack on a display line
ai.stackLead: A new layer does not retire the one below. L0 holds the tool. L1 and L2 score. L3 writes. L4 calls tools. The mura classifier (L2) must be right before a chatbot writes the 8D (L3).

stack.name: Rules and automation
stack.body: No learning. Interlocks, recipes, SPC limits, PLC. Deterministic. Still the last word on a running tool.
stack.line: If CD is over spec, hold the lot.

stack.name: Classical ML
stack.body: Tabular models on sensors, process logs, and yield. Random forests, gradient boosting, residual models. Output is a score or a flag, not a paragraph.
stack.line: FDC flags a chamber drift from 40 traces before the next PM.

stack.name: Deep learning
stack.body: Neural nets on images and sequences. CNNs and vision transformers for inspection; sequence models for traces. This is the production class on a panel photo.
stack.line: AOI labels mura, particle, scratch, or dead pixel.

stack.name: Generative AI
stack.body: Models that create text, code, images, or molecular graphs. LLMs, diffusion, structure generators. Fluent is not the same as true.
stack.line: Draft a 5-why or an 8D D1–D3 from alarm logs. Not a gauge.

stack.name: Agentic AI
stack.body: A planner that uses the layers below: search SOP, query a table, plot, then propose the next check. Read-only first.
stack.line: Pull the last 20 lots, overlay the defect map, list three DOE factors.

ai.eightTitle: 8D is a form, not a model
ai.eightLead: Eight Disciplines problem solving. Used for customer claims and NCR. Generative AI can draft the first pages. It cannot close the file.

eightSteps.name: Team
eightSteps.body: Who owns the file.

eightSteps.name: Problem
eightSteps.body: What failed, where, how many. From MES, AOI, or the claim — not from a caption.

eightSteps.name: Containment
eightSteps.body: What we hold now. Dates and lots from the log only.

eightSteps.name: Root cause
eightSteps.body: Why. Needs data. The model does not invent this.

eightSteps.name: Corrective action
eightSteps.body: What will fix this lot or this cause.

eightSteps.name: Implement
eightSteps.body: Run it. Change control if the process moves.

eightSteps.name: Prevent
eightSteps.body: So it does not come back.

eightSteps.name: Close
eightSteps.body: File and sign. A named engineer.

ai.eightRule: Ask the local model for D1–D3 only. You fill D4–D8 from data. Do not use an 8D as a substitute for AOI pass/fail.
ai.compareLead: The failure modes are not the same, so the review step is not the same.

ai.mlTitle: What ML and DL already do here
ai.mlLead: These systems are not a 2026 story. They are how inspection and equipment health already run. Generative AI does not replace them.

mlItems.title: AOI and defect vision
mlItems.body: Convolutional nets and vision transformers score panel images for mura, particles, scratches, stains, and dead pixels. They are trained on labeled defect libraries. Accuracy is a metrology problem: gold labels, confusion matrices, overkill versus escape.

mlItems.title: FDC and trace anomaly
mlItems.body: Multivariate models watch tool sensors (temperature, pressure, RF, flow). They learn a healthy envelope and fire when a chamber walks. This is classical ML on time-aligned traces, not a chatbot.

mlItems.title: Yield and virtual metrology
mlItems.body: Tabular models map process parameters to electrical or optical results so you do not have to measure every piece. Useful when metrology is slow or destructive. Drift after a part change is the usual killer.

mlItems.title: Predictive maintenance
mlItems.body: Remaining-useful-life models on pumps, robots, and evaporators. The output is a date or a risk score, not a paragraph. Pair it later with generative AI only to write the work order.

ai.genLead: Generation is useful when the output is language, a first draft, or a large design space. It is a poor replacement for a calibrated classifier.

genItems.title: Language on logs and SOP
genItems.body: Summarize a night of alarms, turn a Korean SOP into shop-floor Vietnamese or Chinese, draft 8D and FMEA shells. Always re-check numbers, unit, and spec limits against the source.

genItems.title: Vision-language on a photo
genItems.body: A multimodal model can describe a defect image in words and suggest a class. Treat that as a hypothesis. The production AOI model — trained on your defect taxonomy — remains the system of record.

genItems.title: Virtual images and CD assist
genItems.body: Neural style transfer can build a virtual panel image from a layout plus a real photo, so electrode CD can be compared without extra short-loop hardware. Samsung Display published this as a 2023 industry first.

genItems.title: Materials and code
genItems.body: Molecule-generation plus property and synthesizability models explore OLED stacks far faster than hand design. Coding copilots write Python or SQL against yield extracts so PE/IE time goes to the question, not the boilerplate.

ai.storyLead: A mura cluster on the module line is not an ML problem or a GenAI problem. It is a stacked workflow. Skip a layer and you either miss the defect or ship a pretty, wrong report.

storySteps.title: AOI flags the cluster
storySteps.body: The vision model labels a repeating mura pattern on lots from chamber B. This is detection. Confidence and overkill still belong to the inspection team.

storySteps.title: FDC says the tool is walking
storySteps.body: A trace model shows a slow rise in a deposition sensor over 36 hours — inside spec, outside the healthy envelope. That is prediction, not prose.

storySteps.title: The draft 5-why appears
storySteps.body: An LLM, given the alarm list, the SOP section, and the last similar CAPA, writes three cause hypotheses and the checks for each. Fluent. Still a draft.

storySteps.title: Tools get called
storySteps.body: The agent pulls the last 20 lots, overlays the defect map, and lists three DOE factors. It does not change the recipe.

storySteps.title: Engineer sign-off
storySteps.body: You kill the weak hypotheses, keep one, open change control. AI never bypasses the existing process-change path.

ai.storyClose: If you only deploy chat, you get faster paperwork on top of the same escapes. If you only deploy AOI, you still spend hours writing the story. The leverage is the stack.

rules.when: A repeating signal needs a score or a class
rules.why: Inspection images, traces, yield tables. Train, validate, watch drift.

rules.when: You need a first draft, an explanation, or a translation
rules.why: Reports, SOP Q&A, code, design options. Then a human checks facts.

rules.when: You need detect and then explain
rules.why: DL finds the defect. GenAI writes the deviation. Do not swap them.

rules.when: The next step is a tool call (query, plot, search)
rules.why: Useful for pulling lots and drafting DOE. Not allowed to touch the recipe.

ai.close: FDC and yield sit in machine learning. AOI sits in deep learning. Reports, code, and translations sit in generative AI.

ml.title: Machine learning scores a repeating signal
ml.lead: Machine Learning (ML) maps examples to a number or a class. On a display line that is Fault Detection and Classification (FDC), yield, remaining life — not a paragraph.
intro: You do not write the rule “if pressure > X then alarm.” You show the model many healthy traces and many bad traces. It learns the envelope. That is the whole trick.
Three questions before you trust a score: What is the input? What is the output? How do we know it is still right after a recipe, part, or lighting change?
Deep learning is a kind of ML that learns features from raw images and sequences. This page is the classical layer — tables, traces, and scores. The next page is vision.

ideas.title: Supervised learning
ideas.body: Every example has a label: this lot yielded 97.2%, this trace is “healthy,” this incoming film is “fail.” Most line models live here. The hidden cost is the gold label — who marked it, and how often they disagree.

ideas.title: Unsupervised learning
ideas.body: No label. The model groups lots, chambers, or vendors that look alike. Useful for “what changed this week?” Dangerous if you treat a cluster as a root cause.

ideas.title: Overfitting
ideas.body: The model memorizes last month. Accuracy looks perfect on the training set and collapses the week after a PM or a stack tweak. If it cannot survive a held-out week, it is not a model. It is a diary.

ideas.title: Features
ideas.body: The columns you feed it: sensor stats, recipe IDs, time-of-day, vendor lot. Garbage features make confident, wrong scores. A process engineer who knows which traces actually move CD is worth more than a fancier algorithm.

ml.jobsLead: Name the job before you name the vendor. Each job has a different label, a different metric, and a different failure.

jobs.title: Classification
jobs.body: Assign a class: pass/fail, mura/particle, vendor A vs B risk. Output is a label plus a confidence. The argument is overkill versus escape.
jobs.line: Incoming AOI on film. A tabular model that flags high-risk vendor lots before they enter TFT.

jobs.title: Regression
jobs.body: Predict a number: CD, luminance, yield, remaining useful life. Output is a value you can plot against a gauge. If it cannot beat a simple average, do not deploy it.
jobs.line: Virtual metrology: predict an electrical result from process parameters so you do not measure every piece.

jobs.title: Anomaly detection
jobs.body: Learn a healthy envelope and fire when a chamber walks. Often no “fail” labels — just a lot of normal traces. The fight is the threshold: too tight and you drown in alarms.
jobs.line: FDC on deposition: temperature, rate, and vacuum traces stay inside spec, outside the healthy envelope.

jobs.title: Ranking
jobs.body: Order lots or tools by risk so the scarce inspector or PE hour goes to the top of the list. Not a hard fail. A queue.
jobs.line: Which ten lots from last night should quality re-inspect before ship.

metrics.title: Train, validate, test
metrics.body: Train on past lots. Validate while you tune. Test on a week the model has never seen — after a PM if you can. One accuracy number on the training set is a vanity metric.

metrics.title: Overkill vs escape
metrics.body: Precision is “of the alarms, how many were real.” Recall is “of the real defects, how many did we catch.” On AOI-like tasks, escape costs a customer. Overkill costs capacity. You choose a point on that curve. The model does not.

metrics.title: Drift
metrics.body: A model trained on last year’s stack will silently rot after a material, lighting, or recipe change. Watch the score distribution, not only the dashboard green light. Retrain is a process, not a heroics event.

metrics.title: Always vs a dumb baseline
metrics.body: Compare to last-week average, to SPC, to “always predict pass.” If you cannot beat the baseline on a held-out week, you are adding a black box for no gain.

ml.lineTitle: Where ML already sits at SDV and DSC

lineItems.title: FDC and traces
lineItems.body: Multivariate models on temperature, pressure, RF, flow. They learn a healthy envelope. This is not a chatbot reading a log.

lineItems.title: Yield and virtual metrology
lineItems.body: Tabular models map process parameters to electrical or optical results. Useful when metrology is slow or destructive. Drift after a part change is the usual killer.

lineItems.title: Predictive maintenance
lineItems.body: Remaining-useful-life on pumps, robots, evaporators. The output is a date or a risk score. Pair later with generative AI only to write the work order.

lineItems.title: Incoming and logistics risk
lineItems.body: Vendor-lot scores, pack-damage vision (often DL), ETA risk. Same idea: a number you can threshold.

notItems: Writing an 8D, a 5-why, or a customer letter.
Translating an SOP or explaining a photo in sentences.
Inventing a spec you did not measure.
Replacing interlocks, SPC limits, or change control.
A one-shot model with no owner, no gold set, and no retrain trigger.
checks: Who labeled the gold data, and do two engineers agree on the same lot?
What is the held-out week, and did it include a PM or a recipe delta?
What happens on a false call — hold, re-inspect, or ignore?
What event forces a retrain (stack, lighting, part, vendor)?
Is the baseline (SPC, last-week mean) already good enough?
ml.close: If the output is a score or a class, you are in ML. If the output is a sentence, go to generative AI. If the input is a panel photo, go to deep learning.

dl.title: Deep learning sees the panel
dl.lead: A neural net learns features from pixels and traces. That is why AOI works — and why a lighting change can quietly ruin it.
intro: Classical ML wants columns you already understand: a mean, a max, a recipe ID. Deep learning starts from the raw thing — a photo, a waveform — and learns which patterns matter.
On a display line the main DL job is inspection: mura, particle, scratch, stain, dead pixel. Sequence models also watch traces when the pattern is too rich for a handful of stats.
DL is still supervised most of the time. Someone has to label thousands of defects. The model is only as honest as that library.

ideas.title: Layers instead of hand features
ideas.body: Early layers find edges and blobs. Later layers find “mura in zone C” or “fiber particle.” You do not draw those features. You pay for them with labeled images.

ideas.title: Convolutional nets and vision transformers
ideas.body: CNNs slide small filters across the panel photo. Vision transformers split the image into patches and attend across them. Both can run production AOI. The architecture is less important than the gold set and the lighting.

ideas.title: Transfer learning
ideas.body: You rarely train from zero. You start from a net that already saw millions of public images, then fine-tune on your defect taxonomy. That is why a few thousand well-labeled site images can beat a million random ones.

ideas.title: Sequences
ideas.body: The same idea on traces: a 1D net or a transformer over time. Useful when a chamber failure is a shape in the waveform, not a single threshold.

dl.jobsLead: If you can name the class and you have photos, DL is usually the right layer. If you only have a table, stay on the ML page.

jobs.title: AOI classification
jobs.body: A crop or a full panel in, a class and a score out. This is the system of record for visual defects — not a multimodal chatbot describing the same photo.
jobs.line: Module AOI labels mura vs particle vs scratch. Quality owns overkill vs escape.

jobs.title: Localization
jobs.body: Not only “there is a scratch” but a box or a mask on the panel. Needed when you overlay defects on a layout or on a chamber map.
jobs.line: Repeaters that sit on the same pixel coordinates across lots — a process signature, not random dirt.

jobs.title: Setup measurement from a photo
jobs.body: Vision finds a region and returns a distance. Samsung Display published the Vietnam site case: picker-to-panel style measurements that used to take a person with a gauge.
jobs.line: SDV: 2 min 30 sec → 10 sec on published setup measurement. Fewer bodies near moving parts.

jobs.title: Trace shapes
jobs.body: When FDC stats miss a slow walk that is obvious on a plot, a sequence model can score the shape. Still a score. Still needs a threshold owner.
jobs.line: A deposition rate curve that stays in spec but no longer looks like the golden week.

dl.metricTitle: Why AOI models fail in quiet ways

metrics.title: Gold labels are the product
metrics.body: If two engineers disagree on “mura vs stain,” the net will learn the disagreement. A weekly gold-set review is more valuable than a new backbone.

metrics.title: Class imbalance
metrics.body: True escapes are rare. A net that always says “pass” is 99% accurate and useless. Report escape rate and overkill, not headline accuracy.

metrics.title: Domain shift
metrics.body: New stack, new glass, new lighting, new camera, new product. The pixels changed. The net did not get the memo. Treat a product ramp as a retrain trigger.

metrics.title: Explainability is limited
metrics.body: Heatmaps show where the net looked. They do not replace a metrology reason. Use them to debug the model, not to close an 8D.

dl.lineTitle: Display uses that are already DL

lineItems.title: Panel AOI
lineItems.body: Mura, particles, scratches, stains, dead pixels. Trained on the site taxonomy. Production class stays here even when a generative model captions the same image.

lineItems.title: Incoming film and glass
lineItems.body: Same idea upstream. Catch vendor defects before they become array scrap.

lineItems.title: PPE and zone cameras
lineItems.body: EHS models for helmets, restricted-area entry. A different gold set, the same DL pattern.

lineItems.title: Pack damage
lineItems.body: Logistics vision on cartons and pallets. Score, then a human on the exceptions.

notItems: Drafting the 8D from the defect photo. That is generative AI, after the class is set.
Reading a numeric CD or luminance off a snapshot. Instruments do that.
A weekly report or an SOP translation.
A model with no lighting control and no gold set.
Replacing the AOI owner with a chatbot that “looks pretty sure.”
checks: Is the production class coming from the AOI model, or from a caption?
When did we last refresh the gold set — and did a new product land since then?
What is the escape vs overkill target, written down?
Do we log lighting, camera, and product ID next to every image?
Who has the right to change the threshold?
dl.close: DL finds and scores what is on the panel. It does not write the story. The next page is the story layer — generative AI.

genai.title: Generative AI writes what did not exist yet
genai.lead: It continues a sentence, an image, a molecule. Useful for first drafts. Dangerous as a gauge.
intro: A classifier answers “which class?” A generative model answers “what comes next?” It is paid to finish your prompt with fluent language, pixels, or a candidate structure.
That is why it feels like a colleague and why it will invent a spec that looks local. Fluency is the product. Truth is your job.
On the line the honest uses are drafts, translation, code, virtual images, and material search — always with a human on numbers, and never as a replacement for AOI or FDC.

ideas.title: Tokens, not thoughts
ideas.body: Text is chopped into tokens. The model predicts the next one, again and again. It does not look up your SOP unless you retrieve it — Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). A confident paragraph can still be a chain of likely words.

ideas.title: Context window
ideas.body: Only what you put in the prompt (and what retrieval adds) is in play. Long windows help. They do not replace an indexed, current SOP corpus.

ideas.title: Temperature and sampling
ideas.body: Higher temperature = more variety, more invention. For specs, recipes, and code, keep it low. You want the boring answer.

ideas.title: Hallucination is normal
ideas.body: The model fills gaps. It will quote a limit you never pasted. Treat every number as guilty until it matches SOP, MES, or a gauge.

genai.jobsLead: If the output is language, an image that did not exist, code, or a candidate molecule, you are in this layer. If the output is pass/fail, go back to ML or DL.

jobs.title: Language on logs and SOP
jobs.body: Summarize a night of alarms. Draft 8D and FMEA shells. Turn a Korean SOP into shop-floor Vietnamese or Chinese. Freeze every number.
jobs.line: SDV and DSC shifts can share one SOP if the translation keeps 2.50 mm as 2.50 mm, not 2.5.

jobs.title: Vision-language
jobs.body: Drop a defect photo and a spec snippet in the same prompt. Get a hypothesis and the SOP section to open. The production class still comes from AOI.
jobs.line: Night shift photographs a stain, pastes ten alarms, asks what to check at 08:00. Day-shift owner confirms.

jobs.title: Virtual images and CD assist
jobs.body: Neural style transfer can build a virtual panel image from a layout plus a real photo. Samsung Display published this in 2023 as a CD-measurement assist — generative vision in the service of metrology.
jobs.line: Fewer extra short-loop samples. The virtual width still has to agree with a golden gauge.

jobs.title: Materials and code
jobs.body: Generate / predict / synthesizable loops explore OLED stacks. Copilots write Python or SQL against a yield extract. Chemists and PE still close the loop in a lab or on a copy of the data.
jobs.line: Paste a CSV schema, ask for a 3σ lot list. Read the code. Run it on a copy.

metrics.title: RAG — retrieval first
metrics.body: Search approved SOP, manuals, and CAPA, then write from those passages. Without retrieval the model improvises. With a stale index it quotes last quarter’s limit fluently.

metrics.title: Fine-tune vs retrieve
metrics.body: Fine-tuning changes how the model talks. Retrieval changes what it is allowed to know this week. For SOP, retrieval almost always wins. Fine-tune is for tone and format, not for the current abort limit.

metrics.title: Agents
metrics.body: A planner that calls tools: search, SQL, a plot, a ticket. Useful for “pull last 20 lots and draft the DOE.” Not allowed to write a recipe. Read-only tools first. Log every call.

metrics.title: Multimodal
metrics.body: Text plus image plus, sometimes, a PDF. A caption is not metrology. Pixel pitch, CD, and luminance still come from the instrument.

lineItems.title: Role
lineItems.body: “You are a display process engineer.” It sets jargon and caution. It is not a security control.

lineItems.title: Evidence
lineItems.body: Paste the log, the SOP excerpt, the schema. If a number is not in the prompt, the model must leave a blank — say so.

lineItems.title: Constraints
lineItems.body: Freeze units. Ban invented part numbers. Ask for sources. Ask what is missing.

lineItems.title: Output shape
lineItems.body: Three hypotheses, each with a check. D1–D3 only. A table, not an essay. Shape is how you review.

notItems: A production pass/fail on a panel. That is AOI (DL).
A numeric CD, luminance, or yield taken from a caption.
Pasting unreleased stacks, recipes, customer names, or full MES extracts into a public model.
Closing change control or downloading a recipe to a tool.
A customer report whose numbers you did not re-check against SOP or MES.
checks: Is this a draft, or am I about to treat it as a gauge?
Where did each number come from — prompt, retrieval, or invention?
Is the assistant the approved one, with SOP actually indexed?
Did I strip customer names, unreleased stacks, and operator IDs?
Who signs if this sentence reaches the line or a customer?
genai.close: Generation is leverage on paperwork, translation, code, and search. Detection still belongs to ML and DL.

trends.title: Copilots were last year. Agents are this year.
trends.lead: The models got more multimodal and more willing to use tools. For a display engineer, that means photos, logs, and SOP can sit in one conversation — if you govern the data.
intro: 2023–2024 was chat in a browser. 2026 is models that read a panel photo, search an SOP, write a script, and propose the next measurement. Vendors call this agentic AI.

Adoption in factories is no longer a pilot slide. A 2026 RSM manufacturing survey reported 79% of respondents already using generative AI, with agentic use following. The gap is no longer access. It is judgment: what the model is allowed to see, and who signs the output.

items.title: Agentic AI
items.what: An agent plans steps, calls tools (search, SQL, a plot, a ticket), and returns a recommended action list. It is not a prettier dashboard.
items.whyNow: Tool-use and longer planning finally hold up on messy industrial tasks, not just demo tickets. Samsung Electronics said in March 2026 it will extend agentic AI across manufacturing toward AI-driven factories by 2030.
items.line: “Pull last week’s mura lots on line 2, group by chamber, draft the DOE two-pager.” The agent queries, clusters, writes. You still approve the experiment.
items.watch: An agent with write access is a process-safety issue. Read-only tools first. Log every call. A human owns the change.

items.title: Multimodal models
items.what: One model accepts text, images, sometimes traces or PDFs, and answers in mixed form. You can drop a defect photo and a snippet of the spec in the same prompt.
items.whyNow: Vision-language models are good enough to describe mura texture, particle morphology, and scratch direction — as a second opinion, not as AOI.
items.line: Night-shift engineer photographs a stain, pastes the last ten alarms, asks for likely class and the SOP section to open. The answer is a starting point for the day-shift owner.
items.watch: Pretty descriptions are not metrology. Pixel pitch, CD, and luminance numbers must come from the instrument, not from the caption.

items.title: RAG — answers grounded in your files
items.what: Retrieval-augmented generation searches approved SOP, manuals, and CAPA, then writes the answer from those passages. Without retrieval, the model improvises.
items.whyNow: Long context helps, but a well-indexed SOP corpus is still more trustworthy than hoping the model memorized last quarter’s revision.
items.line: “What is the abort limit on this evaporator after a nozzle change?” The system cites the current Korean SOP and the Vietnamese shop card, with revision IDs.
items.watch: Stale indexes are dangerous. If the SOP moved and the corpus did not, the model will quote the old number fluently. Index freshness is a process owner’s job.

items.title: Coding copilots
items.what: Inline completion, test stubs, SQL, and plot code. The bottleneck in PE/IE is often wrangling the extract, not the statistics.
items.whyNow: Models are competent at pandas, matplotlib, and JMP-like workflows if you paste a schema and a clear question. They still invent column names if you let them.
items.line: Paste a yield CSV schema, ask for a daily trend with a control band and a list of lots outside 3σ. Read the code. Then run it on a copy of the data.
items.watch: Never point a copilot at the production database with write credentials. No customer names, no unreleased stack data in the prompt.

items.title: Reasoning models
items.what: Models that spend tokens on intermediate steps: longer 5-why, FMEA, conflicting-evidence reviews. Slower, better at multi-hop logic than a fast chat model.
items.whyNow: Useful when the task is a structured argument (why this chamber, why not that recipe) rather than a one-line classification.
items.line: Feed two competing CAPAs and the last month of FDC. Ask which hypothesis is still live and which checks would kill it. Treat the chain of thought as a review aid.
items.watch: A longer answer is not a truer answer. Hidden chain-of-thought can still smuggle a wrong unit. Check every number.

items.title: Governance as a feature
items.what: Allow-lists for tools, audit logs, data residency, and “this model may not see this folder.” In 2026 this is part of the product, not a slide after go-live.
items.whyNow: EU AI Act-class rules, customer audits, and a year of leakage incidents made shadow-IT chat a real finding. Approved tools will win over the cleverest public chatbot.
items.line: Use the company-approved assistant for SOP and logs. Public models are for public knowledge only — textbooks, language, generic Python.
items.watch: If a tool cannot show you where a number came from, do not put that number in a customer report.

stats.label: Samsung Electronics target for AI-driven factories across manufacturing.

trends.chartCaption: USD billions. 2023 actual vs 2028 estimate as cited in Samsung Display’s public AI article (USD 3.2B → 20.8B). Directional, not a forecast you should put in a customer deck without the original source.
factoryBody: On 1 March 2026 Samsung Electronics announced a plan to move manufacturing operations to AI-driven factories by 2030. The stated span is inbound logistics, production, quality, and shipment — plus digital twins and specialized agents for quality, production, and logistics.

That is a group-level manufacturing vision, not a site SOP. For display engineers the practical read is: inspection, equipment health, and document workflows will keep absorbing both ML/DL and generative layers. Your job is to know which layer you are touching.
trends.factoryQuote: The next phase of manufacturing innovation lies in building autonomous environments where AI truly understands operational contexts in real time and independently executes optimal decisions.
trends.factoryCite: YoungSoo Lee, EVP, Head of Global Technology Research, Samsung Electronics — 1 Mar 2026
trends.quarterTitle: What to do with this, this quarter
quarterItems: List the three reports or analyses you rewrite every week. Those are GenAI candidates. List the three signals you already score. Those stay ML/DL.
Find the approved assistant and whether SOP retrieval is actually indexed for your line. If it is not, do not fake it with a public model.
Pick one multimodal habit: photo + alarms, never photo alone, and never a number from the caption.

mfg.title: Where each kind of AI attaches to the line
mfg.lead: Every step already has data. ML/DL turns that data into a score. Generative AI turns it into a draft. Agents fetch. None of them own the recipe.
intro: This is not a separate “display industry” tour. You already live on TFT, deposition, module, and inspection. Below is the same value chain with the two AI jobs labeled, plus the three Samsung Display cases that are public.
If a box says ML, someone has to label data and watch drift. If it says GenAI, someone has to check the draft. If it says agent, someone has to deny write access.
mfg.chainLead: Read left to right as product flow. Equipment health and EHS sit across every step.

chain.name: Incoming material
chain.ml: Vendor lot risk, incoming AOI on film and glass, moisture and particle scores.
chain.gen: Translate incoming spec deltas; draft a deviation when a COA is off.
chain.agent: Pull last n lots from a supplier and summarize open NCMRs.

chain.name: TFT / backplane
chain.ml: CD and overlay models, array yield predictors, photo/etch FDC.
chain.gen: Virtual CD images from layout + photo (style transfer). Recipe-change notes.
chain.agent: Cluster scrap by layer and propose the first DOE factors.

chain.name: OLED deposition & encapsulation
chain.ml: Rate and uniformity models, evaporator health, encapsulation leak flags.
chain.gen: Material structure search (generate / predict / synthesizable). Shift-report drafts.
chain.agent: Compare today’s crystal and rate traces to the last golden week.

chain.name: Module
chain.ml: Bond, align, and luminance inspection classifiers.
chain.gen: Customer-facing failure description in EN/ZH/VI from a Korean write-up.
chain.agent: Build a pack of similar returns for the quality meeting.

chain.name: Inspection & quality
chain.ml: AOI taxonomy, escape/overkill trade-off, reliability screens.
chain.gen: 8D / 5-why / FMEA shells from logs plus SOP passages.
chain.agent: Fetch like-defects and the last CAPA, then draft the review pack.

chain.name: Logistics & ship
chain.ml: Pack damage vision, slotting, ETA risk.
chain.gen: Packing instruction translations that keep numbers frozen.
chain.agent: Reslot a hold lot against remaining capacity — proposal only.

chain.name: Equipment health
chain.ml: FDC, remaining useful life, spare-part demand.
chain.gen: Work-order text from alarm codes. Troubleshooting from the manual.
chain.agent: Schedule a PM window against the production calendar — still needs approval.

chain.name: Safety
chain.ml: Camera models for PPE and restricted-zone entry.
chain.gen: Near-miss write-ups and toolbox-talk drafts in local language.
chain.agent: Check open actions before a hot-work permit is issued.

mfg.casesLead: From Samsung Display’s public AI article (2025). No internal yields, no tool IDs. The Vietnam measurement case is the one SDV engineers should be able to retell.

cases.title: Automated setup measurement, Vietnam site
body: Equipment setup used to mean a person measuring distances on the tool — for example picker-to-panel — with the usual time, error, and safety cost of putting a body near moving parts.
The published software lets an engineer capture the scene on a mobile device. Vision models find the measurement region and return the distance.
cases.result: Inspection time 2 min 30 sec → 10 sec. Fewer manual errors, less exposure.

cases.title: Virtual image-based CD measurement
body: Critical dimension checks on electrodes normally want a physical short-loop sample. The published method extracts pattern layout from the design and combines it with a real panel image to synthesize a virtual image for width comparison.
That is generative vision in the service of metrology, not a chatbot. It still has to agree with a golden gauge.
cases.result: Fewer extra samples, shorter development loops — as stated in the public article.

cases.title: Generative design for organic materials
body: Three models: molecule generation, property prediction, synthesis prediction. The chemist sets a skeleton and target properties; the loop proposes structures learned from simulation and experiment.
Manual exploration is a handful of ideas per month. The published system is described as searching millions of structures in the same window. Screening still ends in a lab, not in a slideshow.
cases.result: Search space of candidate OLED materials scaled from hand design to monthly millions.

twinBody: A digital twin is a living model of a tool or a line: recipe, sensors, and constraints, updated from the real process. You try a parameter change in the twin before you spend a lot.

Samsung’s 2030 manufacturing message puts twins together with agents and task robots (line, logistics, assembly, EHS). For display, the honest near-term twin is usually one chamber or one inspection cell, not the whole fab.

twinItems.title: Twin
twinItems.body: Simulate a recipe delta. ML models often sit inside the twin as virtual metrology.

twinItems.title: Agent
twinItems.body: Ask the twin a question in language, get a table and a recommended check — not an auto-download to the tool.

twinItems.title: Robot
twinItems.body: Logistics and hazardous-area sensing. Still a safety-rated system with its own sign-off.

mfg.matrixLead: When someone says “let’s put AI on this step,” ask which column they mean.

play.title: A playbook you can run this week
play.lead: Prompts are not magic. A good prompt is a work order: role, data, constraints, output shape, and what the model must not invent.
intro: Use Qwen, Kimi, or GLM on site. The boxes below are patterns, not a license to paste line data into a public chatbot.
English often produces better code. Your own language is better for shop-floor SOP and for teaching. Numbers, units, and tool IDs must pass through unchanged in every language.

uses: Summarize a night of alarms into three hypotheses with checks.
Draft a DOE one-pager from a defect trend.
Ask what a recipe delta typically moves — then verify in the twin or on data, never from the model alone.
Translate an alarm code into the manual section and the first five checks.
Turn a troubleshooting thread into a clean work order.
Ask for a spare-part narrative only after the PdM model has a score.
8D / 5-why / Ishikawa shells from logs + SOP passages.
Classify a customer complaint sentence into the internal taxonomy, then confirm.
Describe a defect photo as a hypothesis, not as the official class.
Draft a claim timeline with blanks for every date you did not paste.
Python for daily yield, takt loss, and 3σ lot lists.
SQL against an extract, never against production with write access.
Explain a chart in the language of the meeting — after the chart is real.
KO ↔ EN ↔ ZH ↔ VI for SOP and mail, freezing every number.
Meeting notes into action lists with owners.
“What does this abbreviation mean in our process?” — still verify.

play.promptLead: Replace the bracketed fields. Delete anything you would not put in an open ticket. Copy, paste, then edit.

prompts.title: Alarm log → hypotheses
prompts.use: Process / equipment, after a night of trips
prompts.text:
You are a display process engineer. Below is a time-ordered alarm log from one tool. Do not invent sensor names or spec limits that are not in the text.

1) Summarize the sequence in five lines.
2) Give three root-cause hypotheses, each with a check I can run today.
3) Mark any hypothesis that needs data I did not provide.
4) End with a 5-why draft. Leave numbers blank if they are missing.

Log:
[paste]

prompts.title: Defect photo → hypothesis
prompts.text:
You are assisting an AOI engineer. I will attach a panel photo. Our classes are mura, particle, scratch, stain, dead pixel, other.

Return:
- Most likely class, and why (texture, location, shape).
- Second class if the first is weak.
- What the photo cannot tell me (size in µm, layer, electrical fail).
- Three questions I should ask the process owner.

Do not output a numeric CD, luminance, or yield. Those come from instruments.

prompts.title: Yield extract → plot + outliers
prompts.text:
Write Python 3 with pandas and matplotlib only. Columns in the CSV: date, line, lot, yield_pct, defect_ppm, chamber.

- Daily median yield by line, with a band at median ± 3σ of the last 30 days.
- Print lots outside the band.
- Do not invent extra columns.
- Include comments. No file writes except the chart PNG.

Assume the CSV is already loaded as df.

prompts.title: SOP translation, numbers frozen
prompts.text:
Translate the SOP excerpt into clear shop-floor [Vietnamese / Chinese / English / Korean].

Rules:
- Keep every number, unit, tool name, and revision ID exactly as written.
- If a sentence is ambiguous, keep the source in parentheses.
- Use short imperative steps, not marketing language.
- End with a glossary of process terms you kept in English.

Text:
[paste]

prompts.title: Claim + log → 8D D1–D3
prompts.use: Quality, after a customer claim or internal NCR
prompts.text:
You are assisting a display quality engineer. Draft 8D sections D1–D3 only from the claim and the log below. Use Qwen/Kimi/GLM locally — this prompt assumes an on-site model.

Rules:
- Quote the SOP revision if it appears. If it does not, write “revision missing.”
- Do not invent a ppm, a date, a customer name, or a containment action that is not in the text.
- Leave D4–D8 as questions I must fill.
- Flag any cause that is not supported by the log.

Claim:
[paste]

Log:
[paste]

prompts.title: Customer sentence → taxonomy + questions
prompts.text:
You are assisting incoming quality. Classify the customer sentence into our taxonomy: mura, particle, scratch, stain, dead pixel, luminance, other.

Return:
- Most likely class, and the words that drove it.
- What the sentence cannot tell us (layer, size, lot, date).
- Five questions I should ask before I open an 8D.
- Do not invent a lot ID or a ppm.

Sentence:
[paste]

play.englishNote: For code, start in English even if the rest of your day is Korean, Chinese, or Vietnamese. Then comment the script in the language your shift actually reads.

pairs.good: Yield on line 2 module fell 2.1 pp from 10–17 Aug vs the prior 4 weeks. Top defect is mura in zone C. Chamber B deposition. Give three hypotheses and a check for each. Do not invent a spec I did not give you.
pairs.why: Time window, process step, geography of the defect, and a ban on invented specs.

pairs.good: Draft D1–D3 only, using the log and SOP excerpt below. Quote the SOP revision. Leave D4–D8 as questions I must fill. Flag any cause that is not supported by the log.
pairs.why: Limits the model to the evidence you provided and stops it from closing the CAPA in fiction.

pairs.good: Translate to shop-floor Vietnamese. Freeze every number and unit. Keep tool IDs in English. List terms you were unsure about at the end.
pairs.why: A bare “translate” will happily round 2.50 mm to 2.5 mm and drop a revision letter.

play.flowTitle: From alarm to 8D, with the stack
play.flowLead: A full loop so the playbook is not just four text boxes.

flow.title: Detect (ML / DL)
flow.body: AOI or FDC fires. Do not skip this and start from a chat description of the photo.

flow.title: Pack the evidence
flow.body: Log excerpt, SOP section, similar CAPA if you have it, photo. Strip customer names and unreleased stacks.

flow.title: Draft (GenAI)
flow.body: Hypotheses, checks, 8D shell. Prompt as a work order.

flow.title: Fetch (agent, if you have one)
flow.body: Last n lots, defect map, golden-week compare. Read-only.

flow.title: Kill hypotheses (you)
flow.body: Run the checks. Delete what the data does not support. The model does not get a vote.

flow.title: Change control (you)
flow.body: If a recipe, spec, or code moves, use the existing approval path. Paste nothing from a model into a tool.

neverItems: Unreleased stack, recipe, or CD numbers into a public model.
Customer names, device codes, or complaint files that identify a brand.
Full database extracts with operator IDs.
Anything you would not put in an email to a vendor.
play.qualityLead: Inspection still belongs to AOI. These are drafts you can run on Qwen, Kimi, or GLM.

qualityJobs.title: Incoming / OQC
qualityJobs.body: Turn a COA mismatch into a deviation skeleton. List the checks. Do not let the model pass the lot.

qualityJobs.title: In-process escape vs overkill
qualityJobs.body: Ask the model to explain the two errors in shop language. The threshold is still a quality decision, not a prompt.

qualityJobs.title: Customer 8D
qualityJobs.body: D1–D3 from claim + log + SOP excerpt. D4–D8 stay human. No invented ppm.

qualityJobs.title: Claim language pack
qualityJobs.body: KO/EN/ZH/VI reply with frozen numbers. GLM for Chinese, Qwen for mixed languages, Kimi if the pack is long.

guard.title: Fluent is not the same as true
guard.lead: Generative models are paid to continue a sentence. They will finish yours with a spec that looks local and is wrong. The countermeasure is process knowledge plus a closed data path.
intro: ML/DL fails as a wrong score. You can plot that. Generative AI fails as a paragraph that reads like your site. That is harder to catch, and it is why sign-off sits on the engineer, not the model.

risks.title: Hallucination
risks.body: The model invents a limit, a part number, or a “last time we did this” story. Longer answers and confident tone do not reduce this.
risks.rule: Every number in a customer-facing or line-facing document must have a source: SOP revision, MES, or a gauge.

risks.title: Leakage
risks.body: Public chat logs are not your archive. Prompts can be used for training. A screenshot of a recipe is still a recipe.
risks.rule: Only approved assistants see line data. Public models get public knowledge.

risks.title: Drift, for ML/DL
risks.body: A classifier trained on last year’s mura library will silently rot after a stack or lighting change. Generative chat will not notice.
risks.rule: Owners, gold sets, and a retrain trigger belong next to the model, not in a slide.

risks.title: Skipping change control
risks.body: A plausible DOE is still a process change when you run it. Agents that can write to MES or a tool are a safety system.
risks.rule: Read-only by default. Existing change control for anything that moves a recipe, spec, or interlock.

risks.title: Public chatbot instead of local LLM
risks.body: Qwen, Kimi, and GLM are the on-site tools. A personal ChatGPT tab is still leakage, even when the local model is slow.
risks.rule: If the local assistant is down, wait. Quality files do not go to a public log “just this once.”

signBody: AI may draft. It may not release. If a number can scrap a lot or reach a customer, a named engineer confirms it against a system of record.
Your advantage over the model is not typing speed. It is knowing what the chamber sounded like at 3 a.m. and which SOP paragraph is actually in force. That is the review the stack is missing.
guard.nextTitle: Three moves after you close this page

nextItems.title: Find the allowed tool
nextItems.body: Qwen, Kimi, or GLM on site. Ask IT which build is approved. Stop using public chat for anything with a spec, a panel photo, or a customer sentence.

nextItems.title: Pilot one repeating draft
nextItems.body: Pick a weekly report, a translation, or a yield plot. Keep the same prompt for two weeks. Compare time and error rate against the old path.

nextItems.title: Share one good and one bad prompt
nextItems.body: In the team channel, post a prompt that survived review and one that invented a number. That teaches faster than a policy PDF.

start.title: 이미 AI를 쓰고 있습니다. AI 연구자가 될 필요는 없습니다.
start.lead: 삼성디스플레이 베트남(SDV)·DSC(중국 사이트) 품질 엔지니어를 위한 내용입니다. 점수 AI는 초안 AI가 아닙니다. 유창한 문장은 사실이 아닙니다.
intro: 품질 업무는 이미 AI 위에 있습니다. 자동광학검사(AOI)가 패널을 채점하고, 한계가 로트를 잡고, 보고서가 클레임을 설명합니다. 사내 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)인 Qwen, Kimi, GLM이 문장 초안을 씁니다. 검사를 대체하지 않습니다.
신경망을 학습시키거나 학습률을 고를 필요는 없습니다. 필요한 구분은 세 가지입니다. 점수는 문장이 아니고, 유창한 문장은 사실이 아니며, 로컬 모델은 공개 챗봇이 아닙니다.

whoItems.title: 품질 엔지니어
whoItems.body: 수입·공정·출하검사(OQC), 고객 클레임, 8단계 문제해결(8D), 부적합보고서(NCR). 클래스와 숫자와 서명은 당신 것입니다. 모델의 것이 아닙니다.

whoItems.title: 엔지니어, AI 전문가는 아님
whoItems.body: 관리도와 표준작업절차(SOP)는 읽습니다. 역전파를 설명할 필요는 없습니다.

whoItems.title: SDV와 DSC
whoItems.body: 삼성디스플레이 베트남(SDV)과 DSC(중국 사이트). 한국어 SOP, 현장 작업 카드. 규칙은 같습니다.

start.kindsLead: 규칙은 결정합니다. 머신러닝(ML)과 딥러닝(DL)은 점수를 냅니다. 생성형은 초안을 씁니다. 섞으면 캡션이 가짜 임계치수(CD)가 됩니다.

kinds.name: 규칙
kinds.body: CD가 스펙을 넘으면 로트를 잡습니다. 인터록, 레시피, 통계적공정관리(SPC). 학습이 없습니다. 가동 중인 설비의 마지막 말입니다.

kinds.name: 점수 AI (ML / DL)
kinds.body: 많은 예를 본 뒤 클래스나 숫자를 줍니다. 무라 vs 파티클, 위험 점수, 잔여 수명. AOI와 고장검출분류(FDC)가 여기 있습니다.

kinds.name: 초안 AI (생성형)
kinds.body: 없던 것을 씁니다. 8D 뼈대, 번역, 가설 목록. Qwen, Kimi, GLM이 이 일을 합니다. 서명은 사람이 합니다.
kinds.line: 유창함은 참이 아닙니다. 숫자는 SOP, 제조실행시스템(MES), 게이지가 필요합니다.

start.weekLead: “AI 사용률”이라는 새 핵심성과지표(KPI)가 필요하지 않습니다. 초안에 쓰는 시간을 줄이고, 고객 파일에 지어낸 스펙을 0으로 만들면 됩니다.

weekItems.title: 검사
weekItems.body: AOI가 패널을 분류합니다. 생성형은 사진을 가설로 묘사할 수 있습니다. 로트를 닫지는 못합니다.

weekItems.title: 8D와 NCR
weekItems.body: 8D는 클레임·NCR용 Eight Disciplines 양식입니다. 로그와 SOP 발췌를 로컬 모델에 넣습니다. D1–D3만 요청합니다. D4–D8은 데이터로 채웁니다.

weekItems.title: 고객 클레임
weekItems.body: 타임라인과 질문 목록을 초안합니다. 모델이 봉쇄 날짜나 백만분율(ppm)을 만들게 두지 마십시오.

start.termsLead: 이후 페이지는 짧은 형태를 씁니다. 이 목록이 첫 사용입니다.

terms.body: Samsung Display Vietnam. 삼성디스플레이 베트남.
중국 사이트. 중국 현채 품질 엔지니어.
Eight Disciplines. 8단계 문제해결. 클레임·NCR 양식: D1 팀, D2 문제, D3 봉쇄, D4 원인, D5–D8 시정·실행·재발 방지·종결.
Nonconformance Report. 부적합보고서. 로트나 부품이 스펙을 벗어났을 때의 내부 기록.
Automated Optical Inspection. 자동광학검사. 패널 사진의 생산 클래스.
Fault Detection and Classification. 고장검출분류. 걸어가는 설비를 표시하는 트레이스 모델.
Standard Operating Procedure. 표준작업절차.
Manufacturing Execution System. 제조실행시스템. 로트, 날짜, 공식 숫자의 출처.
Statistical Process Control. 통계적공정관리.
Programmable Logic Controller. 프로그래머블 로직 컨트롤러. 인터록이 여기 있습니다.
Critical Dimension. 임계치수. 게이지 숫자이지 캡션이 아닙니다.
Outgoing Quality Control. 출하검사.
parts per million. 백만분율.
Machine Learning / Deep Learning. 머신러닝 / 딥러닝. 점수 AI: 클래스, 점수, 박스.
Large Language Model. 대규모 언어 모델. 사내 Qwen, Kimi, GLM. 초안이지 검사가 아닙니다.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation. 검색증강생성. 인덱스가 있는 것만 인용할 수 있습니다.
Design of Experiments. 실험계획법.
Predictive Maintenance. 예지보전. 잔여수명 점수이지 문단이 아닙니다.
Failure Mode and Effects Analysis. 고장형태영향분석.
라인의 층. L0 규칙, L1 고전 ML, L2 DL, L3 생성형, L4 에이전트.

pathShort.title: 시작
pathShort.body: 청중, 세 가지 일, 품질 한 주.

pathShort.title: 가능 / 불가
pathShort.body: AI가 할 수 있는 것, 없는 것. 생성형도 같은 구분.

pathShort.title: 생성형
pathShort.body: 초안이 실제로 어떻게 만들어지는지. 환각, 검색증강생성(RAG), 작업 지시로서의 프롬프트.

pathShort.title: 실습
pathShort.body: 바로 쓸 품질 프롬프트. 약한 것 vs 나은 것.

pathShort.title: 가드레일
pathShort.body: 서명. 붙여 넣지 말 것. 이번 주에 할 일.

limits.title: AI는 일이 있는 도구입니다. 그 밖에서는 소음이거나 위험입니다.
limits.lead: 프롬프트와 모델 이름보다 먼저: 점수 AI가 할 수 있는 것, 없는 것, 이어서 생성형. 어느 쪽이든 서명은 품질의 것입니다.
intro: 공장의 “AI”는 하나가 아닙니다. 점수 AI(ML/DL)는 반복 신호를 클래스나 숫자로 바꿉니다. 생성형은 없던 문장·이미지·코드를 씁니다. 둘을 섞으면 캡션이 가짜 CD가 됩니다.
limits.aiTitle: AI 전반 — 규칙, 점수, 초안을 같이
limits.aiLead: 이 칸은 스택 전체입니다. 인터록, 자동광학검사(AOI), 고장검출분류(FDC), 사내 대규모 언어 모델(LLM). 쓸모 있습니다. 마법이 아닙니다.

aiCan.title: 반복 결함을 채점
aiCan.body: 무라 라이브러리를 본 AOI는 패널 사진을 분류할 수 있습니다. 학습된 일이지 채팅이 아닙니다.

aiCan.title: 걸어가는 설비를 표시
aiCan.body: FDC는 건강한 범위를 배웁니다. 스펙 안이어도 트레이스가 벗어나면 울립니다.

aiCan.title: 부족한 시간을 줄 세우기
aiCan.body: 재검사할 로트 열 개. 먼저 볼 챔버. 판결이 아니라 대기열입니다.

aiCan.title: 점수 뒤에 문장 초안
aiCan.body: AOI나 로그가 있으면 8D 뼈대나 번역을 쓸 수 있습니다. 초안만.

aiNot.title: 인터록이나 스펙을 대체
aiNot.body: CD가 스펙을 넘으면 로트를 잡습니다. 가동 중인 설비에 모델의 투표권은 없습니다.

aiNot.title: 공정이 바뀐 뒤에도 맞다
aiNot.body: 작년 스택으로 학습한 분류기는 조명·소재·레시피 변경 후 조용히 썩습니다. 누군가 재학습해야 합니다.

aiNot.title: 고객에게 책임지기
aiNot.body: ppm, 날짜, 봉쇄에 서명하는 것은 이름 있는 엔지니어입니다. 모델이 아닙니다.

aiNot.title: 새벽 3시 챔버를 알기
aiNot.body: 사이트 지식이 스택에 빠진 리뷰입니다. AI는 베이를 걷지 않습니다.

aiNot.title: SOP에 없는 한계를 만들기
aiNot.body: MES, SOP, 게이지에 없는 숫자는 숫자가 아닙니다. 우리 글꼴로 쓴 추측입니다.

limits.genTitle: 생성형 AI만 — Qwen, Kimi, GLM, 글을 쓰는 모든 것
limits.genLead: 생성은 첫 초안입니다. 합/불, 계측, 변경 관리에는 틀린 도구입니다.

genCan.title: 8D의 D1–D3 쓰기
genCan.body: 8D = Eight Disciplines. 붙여 넣은 로그와 SOP 발췌로. D4–D8은 데이터로 채울 질문으로 남깁니다.

genCan.title: 하룻밤 알람을 가설로
genCan.body: 원인 세 개, 각각 확인. 빠진 것을 표시. 약한 것은 당신이 죽입니다.

genCan.title: 작업 카드 번역
genCan.body: 숫자, 단위, 툴 ID, 리비전을 모두 고정. 모호한 것은 괄호.

genCan.title: 결함 사진을 가설로 설명
genCan.body: 유력 클래스와 이유. 사진이 말 못 하는 것. 생산 클래스는 여전히 AOI.

genCan.title: 준 스키마로 코드·SQL 초안
genCan.body: 추출 복사본에서. 코드를 읽으십시오. 생산에 쓰기 권한은 없습니다.

genNot.title: 생산 합/불을 주기
genNot.body: 그것은 AOI(딥러닝)입니다. 골드 라벨과 당신이 고른 과검/미검 임계값.

genNot.title: 캡션에서 CD, 휘도, ppm을 읽기
genNot.body: 예쁜 묘사는 계측이 아닙니다. 숫자는 계측기나 MES에서 옵니다.

genNot.title: 변경 관리를 닫거나 레시피를 받기
genNot.body: 유창한 DOE도 실행하면 공정 변경입니다. 기존 승인 경로만.

genNot.title: 이번 주 SOP를 혼자 기억
genNot.body: 검색 없이 즉흥입니다. 낡은 색인이면 지난 분기를 유창하게 인용합니다.

genNot.title: 공개 챗봇에 고객 클레임을 안전하게 두기
genNot.body: “시험만”이어도. 로컬 모델만. 죽어 있으면 기다리십시오.

limits.deskLead: 품질 일을 점수 AI와 생성형에 나눈 표입니다.

deskRows.ai: 가능 — 학습된 AOI, 임계값은 당신 것.
deskRows.gen: 불가. 캡션은 가설.
알람 목록을 요약할 수 있음. 알람이 될 수는 없음.
D1–D3 초안 가능. D4–D8은 당신.
만들 수 없음. 빈칸.
가능. 숫자를 고정하고 다시 읽으면.
승인 불가. 변경 관리는 사람.

testItems: 모델이 내일 사라져도 이 문장을 보내겠는가. 아니면 아직 확인하지 않은 것입니다.
AOI / FDC / MES의 점수인가, 채팅의 문장인가.
모든 숫자: SOP 리비전, MES, 게이지 — 아니면 빈칸.
패널 합/불이라면 생성형 모델은 틀린 도구입니다.
프롬프트에 고객명이 있으면 공개 인터넷을 떠난 것입니다. 사이트의 Qwen / Kimi / GLM만.
limits.close: 점수는 문장이 아닙니다. 유창한 문장은 사실이 아닙니다. 서명은 어느 쪽이든 품질의 것입니다.

tools.title: Qwen, Kimi, GLM을 쓰십시오. 공개 챗봇이 아닙니다.
tools.lead: 사이트에서 로컬 대규모 언어 모델을 돌릴 수 있습니다. 초안을 씁니다. 검사하지 않습니다. 레시피의 공개 인터넷 로그를 보지 못합니다.
intro: 공개 ChatGPT급 도구는 회사 밖에서 학습되고 기록됩니다. 고객 클레임, 스택, 작업자 ID는 — “시험만”이어도 — 거기에 두지 않습니다.
로컬 비서는 Qwen, Kimi, GLM입니다. 유행이 아니라 일로 고르십시오. 셋 다 환각합니다. 로컬은 텍스트가 안에 남는다는 뜻입니다. 참이라는 뜻이 아닙니다.
사이트 IT가 내부 이름을 조금 다르게 불러도 규칙은 같습니다. 승인된 로컬 모델, 공개 붙여넣기 금지, 사람 서명.

whyItems.title: 클레임과 고객명
whyItems.body: 불만 파일은 브랜드를 식별합니다. 공개 로그에 닿는 순간 유출입니다.

whyItems.title: SOP와 한계
whyItems.body: 중단 한계와 작업 카드는 사이트 지식입니다. 로컬 모델은 검색할 수 있습니다. 공개 모델은 보면 안 됩니다.

whyItems.title: 패널 사진
whyItems.body: 불량 사진도 스택, 제품, 고객을 드러낼 수 있습니다. 비전 프롬프트는 승인된 로컬 툴에만.

whyItems.title: 감사
whyItems.body: 품질이 “이 8D 초안을 누가 썼나”를 물으면 답이 사이트 툴이어야 합니다. 개인 계정이 아닙니다.

tools.modelsLead: 능력은 겹칩니다. 벤더 점수표가 아니라 품질 엔지니어용 치트시트입니다. 정확한 빌드는 사이트 IT에 확인하십시오.

긴 컨텍스트. 리비전을 인용하라고 한 뒤 확인하십시오.
